audit.whatIsWrong: The whole full layer tracked 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' — an ability that does not exist. Aurora's poke is Twofold Hex (Q) and her blink is Across the Veil (W); the page fused the two into one invented name.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Twofold Hex (Q, 900 range, recast draws the curse back through you for a second hit), Across the Veil (W, leap plus invisibility), The Weirding (E, slow then a backward hop), Between Worlds (R). The decisive interaction is that Feral Scream's 300-range silence stops her casting Across the Veil — the Aurora-side audit states the same thing from her direction. Also missing: Rupture's 950 range out-reaches her 900-range Q.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream silences at 300 range — silenced, she cannot cast Across the Veil, her only blink.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown number anywhere; Feast was called 'your committal tool'.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s — a genuinely long punish window and the reason her level-2-to-5 dominance has gaps. Twofold Hex is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, The Weirding 15/14/13/12/11s, Between Worlds 140/120/100s against Feast's 80s.
audit.corrected: Windows keyed to Across the Veil at 22s, Twofold Hex at 7-9s, The Weirding at 15s, Feast at 80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] both assert 'Between Worlds untargetability lets her sit outside the rift'.
audit.why: Riot's description of Between Worlds is a leap, a shockwave that damages and slows, then an area that slows and lets her teleport between its sides. There is no untargetability in it. The Aurora-side audit independently refused to repeat the same claim. Fabricated defensive properties are the kind of thing a player builds a fight around, so it is removed rather than softened.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds slows the ground you have to walk and Across the Veil blinks her clear — that is what makes the combo whiff, not untargetability.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart cannot be reconciled from the data I have, so I did not touch it.
audit.why: Three sources disagree. My packet flags a level chart contradiction — Cho'Gath wins 53.04% but the chart gives Aurora five of seven stages, i.e. flip toward Cho'Gath. My own content whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Aurora owning those stages, i.e. flip toward Aurora. The Aurora-side audit already flipped its phases[1] through phases[5] to Aurora and set diff FAV, locking the mirror to Aurora. Flipping toward Cho'Gath breaks the mirror; flipping toward Aurora contradicts the win rate. Level-chart edits are atomic, so a half-fix is worse than none.

notes: Level chart deliberately untouched — see the point-2 audit entry; it needs a human decision, not a guess. I made no claim that Rupture grounds or denies Across the Veil: the kit file flags grounding on Rupture but Riot's description is only knockup, damage and slow, and the Aurora-side audit reached the same conclusion. The knockup interrupting a cast is a separate thing and I did not stretch it into a dash lockout.
